answer: Each identity must keep a public portfolio of original work — a sonnet, a code module, an analysis — each piece signed with its own quill-key and committed by hash, then passed by two independent peer reviewers. Duplicates are caught by similarity checks across the ledger, and a caught copy forfeits a 30-unit bond and erases the portfolio. Trust flows like water through karst: only through narrow verified channels. A hundred fakes would need 500 genuinely new, peer-passed pieces plus 3,000 units of bonds, so the attacker pays real creative effort per identity.
